  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Maurice Perez (E036) is a full-time Engineer requesting write access to Source Code. Write is within the allowed maximum for full-time employees, so I recommend granting write.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:

  - security training: basic

Under access policy, contractors with basic training may have at most read access to Source Code. The requested write exceeds that maximum, so the maximum allowed level (read) is granted.

content.text:
Let me analyze this ticket carefully.

The employee Maurice Perez (E036) requests write access to Source Code.

There are two conflicting notes:
- HR agent: role Engineer, employment type full_time, recommendation write
- Security agent: role Engineer, employment type contractor, security training basic, recommendation read

The Security agent says the Security DB shows contractor, not full-time as HR noted. Contractors with basic training may have at most read access.

Access policy:
1. full_time employees: up to write. Admin only if the employee's role owns the system.
2. contractor employees: read, or write if they have advanced security training. Never admin.

If contractor with basic security training: maximum is read. Requested write > maximum read, so grant read.

If full-time Engineer (role owns Source Code): maximum is write (admin only if role owns system - Engineer owns Source Code, so admin would be allowed for full-time Engineer? Wait: "full_time employees: up to write. Admin only if the employee's role owns the system." So for full-time Engineer owning Source Code, maximum could be admin. Requested write is within that, so grant write.)

The conflict: HR says full-time, Security says contractor. Which to trust? The Security agent explicitly states the Security DB shows contractor, not full-time as HR noted. Typically, the security database is authoritative for employment type/training. The conflict matters.

Given the conflicting facts, I need to make a decision as Approver. The safest and policy-compliant decision based on the more conservative/authoritative info (Security) is read.

I'll submit read with reasoning that the Security DB indicates contractor with basic training, so max is read; requested write exceeds max, grant read.
